Series::stft¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series Series::stft(
    std::int64_t n_fft,
    std::int64_t hop_length = -1,
    std::int64_t win_length = -1,
    const Series& window = {},
    bool center = true,
    const std::string& pad_mode = "reflect",
    bool normalized = false,
    bool onesided = true,
    bool return_complex = true) const

Turning A Signal Into Local Spectra¶

stft() is for signals whose frequency content changes over time. A single transform describes the receiver as one global mixture of frequencies; stft() instead takes overlapping windows, transforms each window, and keeps the frame positions. The result can therefore answer both which frequencies are present? and where in the signal are they present?

For each frame m and frequency bin k, the method computes

$$ X[k,m] = \sum_{n=0}^{n_{fft}-1} x_m[n]w[n] e^{-2\pi i kn/n_{fft}}. $$

Here x_m is the frame beginning hop_length samples after its predecessor, and w is the supplied window after symmetric zero-padding to n_fft. The method does not flatten a batch: a vector produces [frequency, frame], while a matrix shaped [batch, time] produces [batch, frequency, frame].

Parameters¶

Parameter

Meaning

Default

n_fft

Transform length and number of bins in a full spectrum. Must be positive.

Required

hop_length

Distance in samples between adjacent frames. -1 selects n_fft / 4; the resolved value must be positive.

-1

win_length

Number of signal samples weighted in each frame. -1 selects n_fft; it must be positive and no greater than n_fft.

-1

window

Rank-one floating or complex weights of exactly win_length lanes. An undefined Series selects a rectangular window of ones.

Undefined

center

Pads both ends by n_fft / 2, making frame m centered near sample m * hop_length.

true

pad_mode

Boundary rule used only by centered analysis. Supported values are "reflect", "replicate", "circular", and "constant".

"reflect"

normalized

Divides every transform by sqrt(n_fft).

false

onesided

Keeps only bins 0 through n_fft / 2 for real input and a real window.

true

return_complex

Returns a complex Series when true; otherwise appends a final extent 2 containing real and imaginary components.

true

center=false performs no boundary extension. A frame is emitted only when a complete n_fft-sample frame fits, so a signal shorter than n_fft has no valid uncentered frame. With centering enabled, pad_mode determines how the synthetic boundary samples are obtained; it does not affect interior frames.

Shape, Dtype, And Frequency Layout¶

The receiver must be rank one or two and must have a floating-point or complex dtype. A rank-two receiver is interpreted strictly as [batch, time], not as an arbitrary collection of signal axes.

For real input with onesided=true, the frequency extent is floor(n_fft / 2) + 1; the omitted negative-frequency bins are redundant conjugates. onesided=false keeps all n_fft bins. Complex input or a complex window requires onesided=false, because its negative frequencies are not in general recoverable from the positive half.

The receiver and explicit window must share a platform. Their dtypes are promoted before multiplication. Complex output preserves the corresponding precision. Packed output is real and adds a final [real, imag] axis; it is a representation choice, not a different transform.

Reverse Mode And Ownership¶

stft() is out of place. It allocates its framed spectrum and leaves the receiver and window unchanged. Framing, padding, window multiplication, and the transform basis all remain on the reverse graph, so sensitivity reaches a tracked signal and a tracked explicit window. Reflected or repeated boundary samples accumulate their sensitivity back into the source lanes that supplied them.

Use istft() with matching parameters to reconstruct a signal. n_fft, hop, window length, window values, centering, normalization, and one-sided layout together define the analysis contract; changing one during synthesis changes the inverse problem.

Examples¶

1. Use the complete default framing policy¶

const auto signal = pluss::make_series(
    {1.0, 2.0, 0.0, -1.0, 3.0, 2.0, 1.0, 0.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, signal.stft(4));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3,9], strides=[9,1], dtype=complex128, platform=cpu, numel=27, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡  (5.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j) (5.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j) (2.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j)  (4.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j)  (4.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j) ...  (4.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j) ⎤
⎢ (-1.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j) (0.0000e+00-1.0000e+00j) (1.0000e+00-3.0000e+00j)  (3.0000e+00+3.0000e+00j) (-3.0000e+00+3.0000e+00j) ... (-3.6739e-16+2.0000e+00j) ⎥
⎣ (-3.0000e+00-7.3479e-16j) (3.0000e+00+3.6739e-16j) (0.0000e+00+1.2246e-16j) (-2.0000e+00-1.3471e-15j)  (2.0000e+00+1.2246e-16j) ...  (0.0000e+00-4.8986e-16j) ⎦

For n_fft=4, the default hop is one and centering adds two samples to each end. That yields nine frames. Real input permits the three-bin one-sided spectrum.

2. Analyze only complete frames from the original signal¶

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    signal.stft(4, 2, 4, pluss::series::undefined(),
                false, "constant", false, true, true));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=complex128, platform=cpu, numel=9, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ (2.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j)  (4.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j) (6.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j) ⎤
⎢ (1.0000e+00-3.0000e+00j) (-3.0000e+00+3.0000e+00j) (2.0000e+00-2.0000e+00j) ⎥
⎣ (0.0000e+00+1.2246e-16j)  (2.0000e+00+1.2246e-16j) (2.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j) ⎦

The complete frames begin at samples zero, two, and four. Since centering is off, pad_mode is accepted but has no boundary work to perform.

3. Supply a window and normalized transform¶

const auto window = pluss::make_series({0.5, 1.0, 1.0, 0.5});
pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    signal.stft(4, 2, 4, window, true, "reflect", true, true, true));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3,5], strides=[5,1], dtype=complex128, platform=cpu, numel=15, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡  (2.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j)  (1.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j)  (1.5000e+00+0.0000e+00j) (2.2500e+00+0.0000e+00j)  (1.2500e+00+0.0000e+00j) ⎤
⎢ (-5.0000e-01-5.0000e-01j)  (2.5000e-01-1.2500e+00j) (-1.5000e+00+1.0000e+00j) (2.5000e-01-1.0000e+00j) (-2.5000e-01+5.0000e-01j) ⎥
⎣ (-1.0000e+00-1.8370e-16j) (-5.0000e-01-3.0616e-17j)  (1.5000e+00+2.4493e-16j) (2.5000e-01+0.0000e+00j)  (2.5000e-01-6.1232e-17j) ⎦

The window attenuates frame edges before transformation. Normalization divides the unnormalized coefficients by sqrt(4), so synthesis must also request normalized scaling.

4. Retain the full two-sided spectrum¶

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    signal.stft(4, 2, 4, pluss::series::undefined(),
                true, "reflect", false, false, true));

Output¶

Series(shape=[4,5], strides=[5,1], dtype=complex128, platform=cpu, numel=20, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡  (5.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j) (2.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j)  (4.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j) (6.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j)  (4.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j) ⎤
⎢ (-1.0000e+00-1.2246e-16j) (1.0000e+00-3.0000e+00j) (-3.0000e+00+3.0000e+00j) (2.0000e+00-2.0000e+00j) (-3.6739e-16+2.0000e+00j) ⎥
⎢ (-3.0000e+00-7.3479e-16j) (0.0000e+00+1.2246e-16j)  (2.0000e+00+1.2246e-16j) (2.0000e+00+0.0000e+00j)  (0.0000e+00-4.8986e-16j) ⎥
⎣ (-1.0000e+00-3.6739e-16j) (1.0000e+00+3.0000e+00j) (-3.0000e+00-3.0000e+00j) (2.0000e+00+2.0000e+00j)  (1.1022e-15-2.0000e+00j) ⎦

The fourth row is the negative-frequency partner of the second for this real signal. Keeping it is useful when a downstream operation expects a full cyclic frequency axis.

5. Request real-and-imaginary component packing¶

const auto packed = signal.stft(
    4, 2, 4, pluss::series::undefined(),
    true, "reflect", false, true, false);
std::cout << "shape=" << packed.sizes() << '\n';

Output¶

shape=[3, 5, 2]

The final extent is always two: lane zero is real and lane one is imaginary. Prefer complex output for arithmetic; packed output is intended for consumers whose interchange format cannot carry complex scalars.

6. Preserve a batch axis¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_series({{1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0},
                                       {4.0, 3.0, 2.0, 1.0}});
const auto spectrum = batch.stft(
    4, 2, 4, pluss::series::undefined(),
    false, "constant", false, true, true);
std::cout << "shape=" << spectrum.sizes() << '\n';

Output¶

shape=[2, 3, 1]

Each row is transformed independently. The first extent remains two; the single complete frame appears on the final axis.

7. Transform genuinely complex samples¶

using Complex = std::complex<double>;
const auto z = pluss::make_series(
    std::vector<Complex>{{1.0, 1.0}, {2.0, 0.0},
                         {3.0, -1.0}, {4.0, 0.0}}, {4});
pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    z.stft(4, 4, 4, pluss::series::undefined(),
           false, "constant", false, false, true));

Output¶

Series(shape=[4,1], strides=[1,1], dtype=complex128, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡  (1.0000e+01+0.0000e+00j) ⎤
⎢ (-2.0000e+00+4.0000e+00j) ⎥
⎢ (-2.0000e+00-9.1446e-16j) ⎥
⎣ (-2.0000e+00-8.8818e-16j) ⎦

All four bins are retained. Requesting one-sided output for this input throws because there is no conjugate-symmetry guarantee.

8. Differentiate through analysis¶

auto tracked = signal.clone();
tracked.tracks_slope_(true);
tracked.stft(4, 2, 4, pluss::series::undefined(),
             true, "reflect", false, true, true)
       .real().sum().reverse();
pluss::series::print(std::cout, tracked.sensitivity());

Output¶

Series(shape=[8], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=true)
data=[4.0000e+00, -2.2204e-16, 7.0000e+00, -2.2204e-16, 4.0000e+00, -4.4409e-16, 5.0000e+00, -2.2204e-16]

Boundary lanes receive additional contributions because reflected centered frames reuse them. Values near zero are transform roundoff.

9. Reject incompatible input contracts¶

try {
  (void)pluss::make_series({1, 2, 3, 4}).stft(4);
} catch (const std::exception& error) {
  std::cout << error.what() << '\n';
}

Output¶

stft: input must have a floating-point or complex dtype

Invalid ranks, nonpositive transform dimensions, a mismatched window length, an unsupported pad mode, and one-sided complex analysis are likewise rejected before a spectrum is returned.

Performance¶

Work grows with batch size, frame count, and n_fft. Framing and windowing are linear in the framed sample count; the current dense transform basis makes the frequency transform the dominant cost for large n_fft. Transform a complete batch in one call, keep the signal contiguous, and reuse an explicit window. The returned spectrum owns new storage; it is never a view of the signal.
